r-prefill-p8k.caption: Prefill speed for 8K-token prompts of the best commit so far that passes the correctness check, as speedup over the starting code on the same machine; 6-hour runs, 6 with restarts and 9 with LiveLab. Codex: the Codex agent checking each edit with a restart. LiveLab: the same agent, prompt and time budget, checking through LiveLab.

r-megatron.claim: Final speed-up, Codex: 1.15×, 1.08×, 1.09×; LiveLab: 1.11×, 1.10×, 1.07×. No clear winner.
r-megatron.caption: Training speed of the best commit so far that passes the correctness check (its first 40 losses match the reference), relative to the starting code, for each 6-hour run. r-omni.claim: LiveLab 139 vs 152 s per clip (−9%), ahead 92% of the time.
r-omni.caption: Speed per generated clip, best commit so far that passes the full quality check, as measured by the agents' own full checks during the race, as speedup over the starting code's 191.6 s per clip (round 2's START, reference memo off; round 1's 173.5 had it on); one 8-hour race. Codex: the Codex agent checking each edit with a restart. LiveLab: the same agent, prompt and time budget, checking through LiveLab.

r-gqa-kernel.title: Race: attention prefill kernel (GQA)
r-gqa-kernel.claim: LiveLab ahead in 6 of 6 races (+0.08% to +0.67%).
r-gqa-kernel.caption: Both sides run NVIDIA's Kernel Design Agents workflow (KDA); only the checker differs. Best passing check so far in each 2-hour race, one B200 GPU per side. SOL (speed-of-light) score: the benchmark's speed score, 0–1, where 1 is the hardware limit it estimates. Higher is better. Codex: the Codex agent checking each edit with a restart. LiveLab: the same agent, prompt and time budget, checking through LiveLab.

r-moe-fwd-kernel.title: Race: MoE layer kernel, forward
r-moe-fwd-kernel.claim: LiveLab ahead in 5 of 6 races (-4.76% to +4.59%). Live checks are only 2.1× faster here.
r-moe-fwd-kernel.caption: Both sides run NVIDIA's Kernel Design Agents workflow (KDA); only the checker differs. Best passing check so far in each 2-hour race, one B200 GPU per side. SOL (speed-of-light) score: the benchmark's speed score, 0–1, where 1 is the hardware limit it estimates. Higher is better. Kernels that sum with floating-point atomic adds can differ from run to run; if kernels must give bit-identical output on 120 reruns, LiveLab is ahead in 4 and behind in 2. Codex: the Codex agent checking each edit with a restart. LiveLab: the same agent, prompt and time budget, checking through LiveLab.

r-nanogpt.caption: Training time of the best commit so far, re-measured by us in a fresh process (mean over 3 held-out training seeds, reaching validation loss 3.42), as speedup over the starting code's 49.2 s; two 4-hour races. During race 2, another user's jobs shared the GPUs, so it is not a clean repeat (dashed). Codex: the Codex agent checking each edit with a restart. LiveLab: the same agent, prompt and time budget, checking through LiveLab.

m-check-phases-3sys.title: Where one check's time goes in the races: vLLM, FastVideo, Megatron
m-check-phases-3sys.claim: In the paper's own tasks, a restart spends most of a check before the check itself; a live check skips it.
m-check-phases-3sys.caption: Restart vs live for one check, from the races. vLLM: LiveLab's live checks (median of 894); a restart is the same check plus the measured start-up (184 s, the median restart-minus-live gap of the same configuration over 206 restarts), split by phase from 3 restarts with caches kept (weight load, engine init, JIT warm-up; the rest is not split). FastVideo H3: medians of the race's passing full checks (22 Codex restarts, 13 LiveLab live checks). Megatron: race-5 medians (150 restarts, 208 live checks); a restart times steps 31-40 after 30 warm-up steps, a live check steps 5-14 after 4. Hatched: phases the logs do not split.
m-check-phases-3sys.source: v41final + ablation_src DeepSeek ledgers, ablations.json, c2_log.txt; fasth3.json; megatron race5 ledgers

e1-race-check-dots-ordered.title: Every check inside the races (by workload)
e1-race-check-dots-ordered.claim: The four full ML systems: every individual check as a dot, with means and speedup ratios.
e1-race-check-dots-ordered.caption: Same data as e1-race-check-dots for the paper's four full ML systems, in Table 1's order. Codex: the agent restarts a new process per check (OS page cache and on-disk compile caches kept). LiveLab: the same agent, with each edit installed into the running process.

f4-fidelity-systems.title: LiveLab measures what a trusted run measures (the paper's systems)
f4-fidelity-systems.claim: Median live-check error: vLLM -0.2%, Megatron -1.1%, FastVideo (H3) -1.3%.
f4-fidelity-systems.caption: Same data as f3-fidelity-by-task for the paper's full ML systems. Right: checks within ±5% (the band). Points beyond ±10% sit on the edge. Omni has no same-commit pair on disk.
f4-fidelity-systems.source: vllm2.json, v41final ledgers, race5f ledgers, fasth3 official results

m4-model-speed-replay.title: Faster models: the same runs, replayed
m4-model-speed-replay.claim: With an infinitely fast model, the same run shrinks to 5.8 h (Codex) vs 3.6 h (LiveLab) on vLLM, 5.9 h (Codex) vs 5.4 h (LiveLab) on Megatron, 3.4 h (Codex) vs 2.9 h (LiveLab) on FastVideo-T2VA, 5.4 h (Codex) vs 3.6 h (LiveLab) on FastVideo-Ref2VA.
m4-model-speed-replay.caption: Each race run replayed from its own logs with the model's generation k times faster: tool calls keep their logged time, checks keep their logged duration and run one at a time on the arm's GPU in their logged order, and the agent cannot continue past a check's result before the replayed check ends. Only the logged run is replayed; a faster model would also try more, which is not simulated. vLLM and Megatron: 6-hour runs, the best run per side as in the race figures (vLLM: the DeepSeek decode races); FastVideo: one 8-hour run per arm (Omni: round 2). vLLM speed and correctness checks keep their separate GPUs. At 1× each replay is 0.95–1.00 of its logged length.
